name: Lafayette's Virginia force (Continental light infantry, Wayne's Pennsylvania Line and militia)
troop_source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorktown_campaign : "Lafayette, his force grown to about 4,500" (June 1781, after Wayne's 800 and Campbell's 1,000 militia joined). Earlier: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Barren_Hill : "left the Valley Forge camp with 2,400 troops" (May 1778); Virginia detachment began at "about 1,200" (Feb 1781).

rows.label: Landing near Georgetown, SC (North Island)
rows.quote: landed on North Island near Georgetown, South Carolina on June 13, 1777
rows.note: North Island is a barrier island off Georgetown; the pin is the town.

rows.label: Philadelphia (meets Washington)
rows.quote: Lafayette met him at a dinner on August 5, 1777
rows.note: Article says Washington came to Philadelphia to brief Congress; Congress commissioned Lafayette a major general on July 31, 1777.

rows.label: Battle of Brandywine (wounded)
rows.quote: Lafayette first saw combat at the Battle of Brandywine near Chadds Ford
rows.note: Joined Sullivan's division, rallied Conway's brigade, shot in the leg.

rows.label: Skirmish at Gloucester, NJ
rows.quote: defeated a numerically superior Hessian force in Gloucester, on November 24, 1777
rows.note: Led 300 soldiers; article says only 'Gloucester', taken as Gloucester City NJ (Delaware River, opposite Philadelphia).

rows.label: Leaves Valley Forge for Barren Hill
rows.quote: On May 18, Lafayette left the Valley Forge camp with 2,400 troops
rows.note: Marquis de Lafayette article gives 2200 men; Barren Hill article gives 2,400.

rows.label: Barren Hill (escapes British encirclement)
rows.quote: Lafayette calmed his retreating force and slipped away with relatively few casualties
rows.note: Battle date May 20 from same article; he took up position there on May 18.

rows.label: Englishtown (advance force before Monmouth)
rows.quote: By June 27, Lafayette was safely back in the fold
rows.note: Quote continues 'with what was now Lee's vanguard of some 4,500 troops at Englishtown'.

rows.label: Battle of Monmouth
rows.quote: Lafayette sent a message to Washington to urge him to the front
rows.note: Marquis article puts him on the field June 28; Monmouth article also describes part of his force retreating that morning.

rows.label: Rhode Island expedition (Estaing off Point Judith)
rows.quote: immediately met with Generals Greene and Lafayette
rows.note: Estaing arrived off Point Judith July 29 and met Greene and Lafayette; meeting place not stated; Point Judith pin is approximate (Newport area). Lafayette led about 3000 men per the Marquis article. Battle of Rhode Island (Aug 29) omitted: he was sent to Boston and the article does not place him in the fighting.

rows.label: Boston (returns from France on the Hermione)
Morristown (reunion with Washington)
rows.quote: on May 10, 1780, had a joyous reunion with Washington at Morristown, New Jersey

rows.label: Peekskill (sets out for Virginia)
rows.quote: Lafayette, who left Peekskill, New York the same day
rows.note: Same day as Congress authorised the Virginia detachment (Feb 20); about 1,200 light infantry.

rows.label: Head of Elk (his force arrives)
rows.quote: Lafayette's force reached Head of Elk
rows.note: Article says his force; he commanded the expedition. Head of Elk is present-day Elkton, MD.

rows.label: Yorktown (inspects situation with Steuben)
rows.quote: Lafayette traveled south, reaching Yorktown on March 14
rows.note: He went ahead from Annapolis while his troops awaited transport.

rows.label: Richmond (withdraws as Cornwallis advances)
rows.quote: On May 24, he set out after Lafayette, who withdrew from Richmond
rows.note: Yorktown campaign article: Cornwallis reached Petersburg May 19, prompting Lafayette to retreat to Richmond. Exact arrival date not stated (late April per general accounts, unsourced here), so only this date is used.

rows.label: Battle of Green Spring (Jamestown)
rows.quote: When Lafayette came up with his main force
rows.note: Lafayette was present and was unhorsed during the retreat; Wayne led the advance. No event id exists for this battle.

rows.label: Siege of Yorktown (assault on the redoubts)
rows.quote: Lafayette's 400 men on the American right took Redoubt 9
rows.note: Sources disagree on the redoubt: the Siege of Yorktown article says a French column took No. 9 and Hamilton took No. 10. Row marks Lafayette's presence in the siege lines only.

rows.label: Boston (sails for France)
rows.quote: Lafayette left Boston for France on December 18, 1781
